authors: Oskar Wage, Udo Feuerhake, Artem Leichter
name: luh-parking-locations-and-utilization-from-lidar-mobile-mapping-surveys
notes:
**Work in progress: data might be changed**

The data set contains the locations of public roadside parking spaces in the northeastern part of Hanover Linden-Nord. As a sample data set, it explicitly does not provide a complete, accurate or correct representation of the conditions! It was collected and processed as part of the 5GAPS research project on September 22nd and October 6th 2022 as a basis for further analysis and in particular as input for simulation studies. 


## [Vehicle Detections](https://data.uni-hannover.de/dataset/parking-locations-and-utilization-from-lidar-mobile-mapping-surveys/resource/4c8d2aff-4db0-481f-83a7-6830c918dd83)

Based on the mapping methodology of Bock et al. (2015) and processing of Leichter et al. (2021), the utilization was determined using vehicle detections in segmented 3D point clouds. The corresponding point clouds were collected by driving over the area on two half-days using a [LiDAR mobile mapping system](https://www.ikg.uni-hannover.de/de/forschung/laserscanning/laserscanning-detail/projects/lidar-mobile-mapping), resulting in several hours between observations. Accordingly, these are only a few sample observations. The trips are made in such a way that combined they cover a synthetic day from about 8-20 clock.  

The collected point clouds were georeferenced, processed, and automatically segmented semantically (see Leichter et al., 2021). To automatically extract cars, those points with car labels were clustered by observation epoch and bounding boxes were estimated for the clusters as a representation of car instances. The boxes serve both to filter out unrealistically small and large objects, and to rudimentarily complete the vehicle footprint that may not be fully captured from all sides.

![Overview map of detected vehicles](https://data.uni-hannover.de/dataset/0945cd36-6797-44ac-a6bd-b7311f0f96bc/resource/807618b6-5c38-4456-88a1-cb47500081ff/download/detection_map.png "Overview map of detected vehicles")
Figure 1: Overview map of detected vehicles


## [Parking Areas](https://data.uni-hannover.de/dataset/parking-locations-and-utilization-from-lidar-mobile-mapping-surveys/resource/68d5a85f-e52d-4328-b24f-a29faa0a62d0)

The public parking areas were digitized manually using aerial images and the detected vehicles in order to exclude irregular parking spaces as far as possible. They were also tagged as to whether they were aligned parallel to the road and assigned to a use at the time of recording, as some are used for construction sites or outdoor catering, for example. Depending on the intended use, they can be filtered individually.

![Example parking area occupation pattern](https://data.uni-hannover.de/dataset/0945cd36-6797-44ac-a6bd-b7311f0f96bc/resource/16b14c61-d1d6-4eda-891d-176bdd787bf5/download/parking_area_example.png "Visualization of example parking areas on top of an aerial image [by LGLN]")
Figure 2: Visualization of example parking areas on top of an aerial image [by LGLN]


## [Parking Occupancy](https://data.uni-hannover.de/dataset/parking-locations-and-utilization-from-lidar-mobile-mapping-surveys/resource/17eb598e-b8b7-4808-9733-8cb0af16a345)

For modelling the parking occupancy, single slots are sampled as center points every 5 m from the parking areas. In this way, they can be integrated into a street/routing graph, for example, as prepared in Wage et al. (2023). Own representations can be generated from the parking area and vehicle detections. Those parking points were intersected with the vehicle boxes to identify occupancy at the respective epochs. 

![Overview map of parking slots' average load](https://data.uni-hannover.de/dataset/0945cd36-6797-44ac-a6bd-b7311f0f96bc/resource/ca0b97c8-2542-479e-83d7-74adb2fc47c0/download/datenpub-bays.png "Overview map of parking slots' average load")
Figure 3: Overview map of average parking lot load

However, unoccupied spaces cannot be determined quite as trivially the other way around, since no detected vehicle can result just as from no measurement/observation. Therefore, a parking space is only recorded as unoccupied if a vehicle was detected at the same time in the neighborhood on the same parking lane and therefore it can be assumed that there is a measurement. 

To close temporal gaps, interpolations were made by hour for each parking slot, assuming that between two consecutive observations with an occupancy the space was also occupied in between - or if both times free also free in between. If there was a change, this is indicated by a proportional value. To close spatial gaps, unobserved spaces in the area are drawn randomly from the ten closest occupation patterns around.

This results in an exemplary occupancy pattern of a synthetic day. Depending on the application, the value could be interpreted as occupancy probability or occupancy share. 

![Example parking area occupation pattern](https://data.uni-hannover.de/dataset/0945cd36-6797-44ac-a6bd-b7311f0f96bc/resource/184a1f75-79ab-4d0e-bb1b-8ed170678280/download/occupation_example.png "Example parking area occupation pattern")
Figure 4: Example parking area occupation pattern

resources.description:
Public parking bay centers with occupation info:

* aid [integer]: parking area id
* bid [integer]: parking bay id in area
* geometry [well-known-text point geometry]: location of bay in EPSG:25832 CRS
* load_avg [float]: average load/occupation
* load_h [dict-map of floats]: interpolated load/occupation by hour of day

For background info, please see general description.

resources.description:
Defined public parking areas:

* id [integer]: element index
* alongside [bool]: parking orientation to street
* type [string]: category of restriction *
* geometry [MultiPolygon]: area in EPSG:25832


(*) categories:

* parking: allowed for parking
* stopping: allowed for stopping
* logistics: reserved for logistics
* informal: informally used for stopping/parking
* reserved: reserved for handicapped parking etc.
* construct: blocked for construction site
* gastro: blocked for outdoor catering/seating

For background info, please see general description.
